title: Land ARBITRATION S37 — infoFor() becomes first-match-wins, and the merge order becomes declared
measured_at: dea6517 and later (the tree moved under me — see tree_drift)
ruling: corpus/00-doctrine/ARBITRATION.md S37. RI-DLG01 §A governs; the engine yields. Not mine to revisit.
next_step: critic round; then the two hand-offs below (stale instruments; the manifest reorder question)

acceptance.before: GATE FAIL — 58 resolutions, 37 speaker/topic pairs, 8 topics, exit 1 (reproduced the ruling exactly at session start)
acceptance.after: GATE PASS — first admissible info in authored order on all 42,456 resolutions, exit 0
acceptance.self_test_before: 4/4 arms as predicted, exit 0. baseline divergence 1,906,688 / 1,460,324,864 — the ruling's number, reproduced
acceptance.self_test_after: 4/4 arms pass, exit 0. ARM 4a now reports the shipped reader agreeing (0 mismatches), which is the documented post-landing behaviour
acceptance.sabotage_arm: reference rule replaced by the shipped rule on a SCRATCH COPY (tools/dialogue/arbiter-* never edited): ARM 2 FAILED, exit 2. Watched going red before I trusted it.

what_i_changed.1_selection_rule: game/src/character/converse.js infoFor(): scoring DELETED (not re-weighted) — `best = info; break;`. The 8/2/4/(1+d/100)/0.5 weights, `bestScore`, and the whole scoring rationale comment are gone. infoAllowed(), the npc-own-line short-circuit, the canon register, the cell prefix match, the actor filter and the entire return literal including `to` are untouched, per the ruling: those are FILTERS, only the CHOICE was in dispute.
what_i_changed.2_declared_merge_order: game/data/dialogue/topics/_manifest.json — the declared order of all 21 topic files, keyed on the per-file `group`. buildTopicIndex() orders docs by it and by nothing else, so every consumer (engine, gate, census, lint) resolves against one sequence. Registered in game/data/index.json so the engine loads it too.
what_i_changed.3_fail_closed: A topic file whose `group` is not in the manifest is an ERROR, and a corpus doc list with no manifest is an ERROR. A hand-built fixture with no `group` anywhere passes through untouched, so bare unit tests are unaffected (RULES 13 — deliberately narrow).
what_i_changed.4_order_infos: tools/dialogue/order-infos.mjs — header rewritten (its stated rationale was written on the losing side and was false as of S37), and `--verify-inert` IMPLEMENTED. It was cited in that header as the proof the reordering was inert and it did not exist anywhere in the file.

the_finding_worth_reading.what: S37 says the merge order was inherited from readdirSync().sort(). It was worse than that: it was inherited from TWO different sorts that disagreed with each other.
the_finding_worth_reading.detail: Every tool built its doc list with readdirSync().sort() — by FILENAME. The engine built its with Object.keys(out.topics).sort() (game/src/engine.js loadData), keyed on `doc.id || basename`. Three of the 21 topic files carry a top-level `id` (06-opening-roots, 45-speaker-coverage, main-quest-argument), so each sat in a different position in the running game than in every instrument pointed at it. 36 of the 92 multi-file topic ids involve one of those three.
the_finding_worth_reading.measured: node tools/dialogue/s37-merge-order-consume.mjs --pre <pre-manifest reader>. Before the manifest: 5,760 of 2,414,880 answers differ in 9 topics between the engine's arrival order and the tools'. After: 0 in 0 topics, and still 0 from a deliberately reversed arrival order.
the_finding_worth_reading.example: soulrest-customs-clerk on `background` said one thing in the game and a different thing in every measurement of the game.
the_finding_worth_reading.why_it_matters: Under the scoring reader this was survivable because order only broke ties. Under first-match-wins the order IS the algorithm, so the shipped game and its own gate were resolving two different corpora.

consumption_RI_MTH07.arms: ARM 1 shipped reader: arrival order inert (0 / 2,414,880, twice). ARM 2 CONTROL, pre-manifest reader: 5,760 differ (engine vs tool order) and 15,460 differ (reversed vs tool order) — WATCHED GOING RED. ARM 3 fail-closed: unlisted file rejected, missing manifest rejected, hand-built fixture still loads.

delete_the_fix.shape: 2x2 — selection rule x declared merge order. Not an inert fix and not two-guards-for-one-defect: the SELECTION RULE moves both numbers on its own, and the manifest moves neither through this instrument (by design — it ratifies the order the tools already used; its effect is on the ENGINE's arrival order, which the gate does not exercise and which the consumption tool above measures separately).
delete_the_fix.control_watched_red: YES — arms A and B both fail the gate. The teardown was verified to actually differ from the shipped file (byte compare + anchor assertion) before it was trusted, so it is not an inert control.
delete_the_fix.teardown_location: scratch copies outside the repo. tools/dialogue/arbiter-* was never edited.

unhearable_infos.instrument: node tools/dialogue/s37-unhearable.mjs — NEW, and it CALLS infoFor() rather than modelling it
unhearable_infos.why_5_not_6: tree drift, not a discrepancy. W1-17-r2 landed 105 INFOs given a body, 20 re-homed, and cut `res`/`q`; speakers went 347 -> 369. Both of my ends are measured with the same instrument on the same tree, so the +5 is internally consistent. The arbiter's own section E independently reports 8 -> 13 on today's tree, so two instruments agree.
unhearable_infos.diagnosis: ALL FIVE are shadowed ACROSS THE MERGE BOUNDARY, not inside a file. In every case a broader same-actor entry in an EARLIER file (50-mainline, 50-factions, 10-global) precedes a more specific entry (`d`, `cell`) in a LATER file (70-disputes, 55-utility). Within each file the order is correct — the corpus is at order-infos' fixed point. order-infos.mjs sorts WITHIN a topic record and structurally cannot see cross-file shadowing, which is where 100% of the remaining §D violations now live.
unhearable_infos.corroboration: tools/dialogue/shadow-audit.mjs independently reports 5 shadows 'audited against the shipped reader; 5 genuinely unreachable'. tools/dialogue/build-graph.mjs reports 5 unreachable INFOs. I do NOT claim build-graph's delta as mine — I have no clean before for it.
unhearable_infos.not_repaired: Deliberately. The ruling prices this cost and says the repair is to reorder the files, and S37 'WHAT THIS DOES NOT DECIDE' item 7 leaves which answer is better to whoever reorders. I landed the cost and named it rather than hiding it.

order_infos_verdict.question_asked: is the authored order order-infos --write produced actually better?
order_infos_verdict.answer: Within a file: yes, and it is now verifiable for the first time. Across files: the tool has no opinion at all, and that is where every remaining defect is.
order_infos_verdict.re_run: node tools/dialogue/order-infos.mjs reports 0 topic(s) across 0 file(s) out of 353 multi-info topics — the corpus is already at the tool's fixed point from an earlier --write, so --write is a no-op today. I did NOT run --write; there was nothing for it to do.
order_infos_verdict.the_control_is_no_longer_vacuous: --verify-inert (implemented this round): 0 of 2,414,880 answers change. --verify-inert --break: 33,030 of 2,414,880 change across 36 topics. Under the old rule authored order decided 0.018% of resolutions in ONE topic, so this measurement could not have come out any other way; it can now.
order_infos_verdict.the_86_5_percent: The 86.5%-already-sorted / 13.5%-not figures are from 63f41ef, BEFORE order-infos --write ran. The 13.5% were rewritten then. I cannot cleanly re-judge 'better' against the pre-tool corpus because that corpus also predates W1-17-r2's 125 content changes, and comparing across both would conflate ordering with content. Said plainly rather than fudged.

hand_offs.what: Two dialogue instruments MODEL the deleted scoring rule instead of calling the reader, and are now measuring an algorithm that does not exist.
hand_offs.detail: tools/dialogue/critic-reach.mjs hard-codes the 8/2/4/d/0.5 weights at its line 111 and sorts by them at 133. Its output is byte-identical before and after this change (6 unhearable, causes reading 'always outscored' — nothing is outscored by anything now). tools/dialogue/critic-semantics.mjs does the same at its line 81 and now FAILS with 206 divergences, comparing two MODELS while never touching infoFor().
hand_offs.why_i_did_not_fix_them: Not my files. W1-17-r2 owns both, has finished, and its published 136 -> 6 headline is measured with critic-reach — repairing it would retroactively move another piece's number, and RULES 22/25 say I do not grade that work. Reported, not touched.
hand_offs.note: This is exactly what the W1-17 round-1 critic predicted: 'every instrument in this round was built on the losing side of that disagreement.'

hand_offs.what: Now that the merge order is declared, the W1-17 round-1 hard fail is a one-line fix — promote main-quest-argument above 50-mainline in the manifest. Recorded as an open question IN the manifest, not taken.
hand_offs.quantified: Separately measured: promoting 70-disputes and 55-utility above 50-factions/50-mainline takes unhearable 13 -> 10. It rescues 4 of the 5 newly-dead, creates a new one (the-witness#5), and does not fix the-xanmeers#3. A real lever, not a free one — which is why it is an authoring judgement and not mine.

tree_drift: A dozen agents are live and the tree moved under me repeatedly. Two consequences worth recording. (1) The gate baseline moved 58 -> 48 mismatches for the SCORING reader between my first run and my 2x2; arms A and B are identical (48/48), which proves the shift was other agents' corpus edits and not my manifest. (2) tools/bank.mjs committed my converse.js MID-EDIT at bf4ec20, in a state with `bestScore` removed from the declaration but still referenced in the loop, so HEAD carried a converse.js that threw ReferenceError for anyone importing it. Confirmed by running it. My working tree was always correct throughout. The broken window was bf4ec20 -> f291b01 and was closed by a LATER BANK COMMIT that picked up my finished tree, not by my own commit cc70ad2 — I first recorded that my commit repaired it, checked, found that wrong, and corrected it here and in the survey. Not a neighbour's fault and not mine — it is RULES 17's documented bank behaviour, recorded so the next agent who sees a broken HEAD knows what it was.
consumers_swept: 13 buildTopicIndex consumers run after arming the fail-closed assertion (consume, root-coverage, critic-semantics, build-graph, critic-reach, answer-census, shadow-audit, critic-field-census, order-infos, critic-w1-07-r3b, canon-consumption, topic-supply-audit, tribe-census). NONE is broken by the manifest assertion. One WAS, during the change — check-dialogue-topics filters docs on Array.isArray(doc.topics) and dropped the manifest, after which buildTopicIndex fail-closed and took the gate down. Fixed by giving the manifest an empty `topics: []`, which neutralises that whole class of filter. RULES 13, learned the hard way and written into the manifest so it is not relearned.

I add no NPC records and re-home nothing; it changed no ordering code. Ran node tools/ownership.mjs --for game/data/dialogue/ before touching anything.
